sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 289, recorded on May 27th, 2026.

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Ben, we get an update on Ben's thoughts on AI, the first since August of 2025.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我的联合主持人是本，我们将了解本对人工智能的最新看法，这也是自 2025 年 8 月以来的首次。

sentences.en: I was talking to Jason a couple of months ago at a meetup.

sentences.en: Jason Turner for potentially irregular listeners.

sentences.en: Yes, but continue.

sentences.en: And I was saying to him, like, we were talking about, like, how should we think about the effects of AI in this area, about the atrophy of skills or whatever.

sentences.en: And he made an interesting analogy, which is that, you know, so to a first approximation, today, one cannot buy good quality furniture.

sentences.en: Now, on the flip side, you know, the average person earning the median wage can, you know, can go and buy bookcases at Ikea and have a good life with them,

sentences.en: have a better life with them, right?

sentences.en: But still, there's a market for high quality furniture, right?

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: It's now a high-end market.

sentences.en: And I don't want to turn this into the couch episode, but just to say that.

sentences.en: And so, you know, maybe, maybe this is the way that software engineering is going.

sentences.en: Maybe, maybe these AI tools increase the ability of less experienced people to get what they need done with software, right?

sentences.en: But, but also maybe they compress or, or sort of hyper-extend the tail of, of, of our ability to actually write good quality software

sentences.en: and the number of practitioners who are doing that in future.

sentences.en: Well, this is great folks.

sentences.en: I see.

sentences.en: It's just this kind of extreme capitalism society we're now living in, where wealth is so concentrated that it is, you know, people and companies are now outside of the law.

sentences.en: Like, just ask yourself what effect AI is currently having on the, for example, the free software slash open source world that is the bedrock,
sentences.zh: 比如，只要问问自己，人工智能目前对自由软件/开源世界产生了什么影响，这在许多方面是

sentences.en: And it's also, since it's so easy to copy, once you can, once you see, once you see the behavior of a system, if you can ask your AI to regenerate it,

sentences.en: that means trade secrets are also out the window.

sentences.en: That means, you know, and, and, and basically,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，你知道，而且，基本上，

sentences.en: And to my mind, the, the only currently defensible position is to simply not take any AI contributions.

sentences.en: I don't, do you actually know what most?

sentences.en: So that is just talking about sort of the, the, the one form of the legal concerns.

sentences.en: Of course, the, the other side is that I, you know, to ask another question, a question, which might make, might make people feel uncomfortable.

sentences.en: You know, the question that JF Bastian asked in a talk a couple of years ago, have you ever written code that killed someone unintentionally?
sentences.zh: 你知道，JF 巴斯蒂安（JF Bastian）几年前在一次演讲中提出的问题：你有没有写过无意中杀死人的代码？

sentences.en: And, you know, I work on power management code inside the Intel CPU package.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我在英特尔 CPU 封装内部从事电源管理代码的工作。

sentences.en: If my code fails, it could kill someone or contribute to it.
sentences.zh: 如果我的代码失败了，可能会害死人或间接导致人员伤亡。

sentences.en: When I was writing in games, I didn't have these, when I was writing games, I didn't have these concerns pretty much by and large.

sentences.en: Now I've moved further into like being actually in part responsible for human life, it seeMs. And so I really do have a moral responsibility.

sentences.en: That is, I mean, I've mentioned when I talked to a few people that as much as people might be excited about AI coding, there's always going to be, you know,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，正如我与一些人交谈时提到过的，尽管人们可能对人工智能编程感到兴奋，但总会存在，你知道的，

sentences.en: If you've got some AI system helping contribute like design stuff.

sentences.zh: 无论如何，如果你是用感觉胡乱编写你自己的个人 link tree 网站，我自己也做过，你

sentences.en: know, that's not going to hurt anybody, but all software is not like that.

sentences.en: It's kind of a cliche that, you know, engineers, software engineers, people who know how the sausage is made oftentimes are much more cherry about the devices in their homes.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 比如，毫无疑问，人工智能在许多领域是一个有用的工具。

sentences.zh: 我看到它非常有用地方之一是在诊断方面，对吧？
